title.es: Aunque, mientras que y a pesar de

es: Reconocer cómo although, whereas, despite e in spite of unen dos ideas contrarias y con qué estructura se usa cada uno.

teaching.en: Although the old town is crowded, it is my favourite place.
teaching.es: Aunque el casco antiguo está abarrotado, es mi lugar favorito.
teaching.explanationEs: Although + sujeto + verbo: presenta un dato que contrasta con lo que sigue.
segments: Although the old town is crowded,
teaching.audioText: Although the old town is crowded, it is my favourite place.

teaching.en: The centre is noisy, whereas the park is quiet.
teaching.es: El centro es ruidoso, mientras que el parque es tranquilo.
teaching.explanationEs: Whereas contrasta dos cosas distintas. No expresa sorpresa, sino comparación.
teaching.audioText: The centre is noisy, whereas the park is quiet.

teaching.en: Despite the heavy traffic, we arrived on time.
teaching.es: A pesar del tráfico denso, llegamos a tiempo.
teaching.explanationEs: Despite + sustantivo: el tráfico. No lleva sujeto + verbo.
teaching.audioText: Despite the heavy traffic, we arrived on time.

teaching.en: In spite of being expensive, the hotel is always full.
teaching.es: A pesar de ser caro, el hotel siempre está lleno.
teaching.explanationEs: In spite of + -ing: equivale a despite y tiene el mismo uso.
teaching.audioText: In spite of being expensive, the hotel is always full.

teaching.en: Despite the fact that the street is narrow, buses use it.
teaching.es: A pesar de que la calle es estrecha, los autobuses la usan.
teaching.explanationEs: Despite the fact that + sujeto + verbo: cuando quieres una cláusula completa.
segments: Despite the fact that the street
teaching.audioText: Despite the fact that the street is narrow, buses use it.

teaching.en: The square is famous, although few tourists visit it.
teaching.es: La plaza es famosa, aunque pocos turistas la visitan.
teaching.explanationEs: Although también puede ir en medio de la frase, con coma delante.
teaching.audioText: The square is famous, although few tourists visit it.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase une las dos ideas como contraste entre dos lugares?

choices.text: The beach is crowded, whereas the park is empty.
The beach is crowded despite the park is empty.
The beach is crowded although the park.

feedback.es: Whereas compara dos cosas distintas, la playa abarrotada y el parque vacío, y va con sujeto + verbo.

hint.es: Son dos lugares distintos: el conector va seguido de sujeto + verbo.

origin.text: The beach is crowded. The park is empty.

prompt.es: Completa: «Aunque el tren es caro, siempre está lleno.»

feedback.es: Although introduce un dato que contrasta con lo que sigue y lleva sujeto + verbo: the train is expensive.

prompt.es: Completa: «A pesar del ruido, dormimos bien.»

hint.es: Después viene un sustantivo, no sujeto + verbo.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase une las ideas con un contraste correcto?

feedback.es: Although une una idea sorprendente con otra y lleva sujeto + verbo: a Leo le gusta el casco antiguo aunque esté lleno de gente. Despite no admite sujeto + verbo y whereas compara dos cosas distintas.

origin.text: Leo likes the old town. It is very crowded.

es: Unir dos oraciones en una con who, which, whose, participio de presente o participio de pasado para añadir información extra.

teaching.en: The old bridge, which crosses the river, is 200 years old.
teaching.es: El viejo puente, que cruza el río, tiene 200 años.
teaching.explanationEs: Which + verbo añade un dato sobre una cosa. Va entre comas y se puede quitar.

teaching.audioText: The old bridge, which crosses the river, is 200 years old.

teaching.en: Mr Lopez, who owns the bakery, knows every neighbour.

accepted: Although my neighbourhood is small, it is very lively. The library, which is on the corner, is always full of children. Mrs Rojas, who runs it, knows all the residents. Despite the traffic, the park, built last year, is peaceful, whereas the centre is noisy.

Although my neighbourhood is small, it is lively. The library, which is on the corner, is always full of children. In spite of the traffic, the park, opened last year, is quiet, whereas the centre is noisy. Mrs Rojas, who runs the library, knows everyone.

feedback.es: Un buen párrafo mezcla estructuras: although o whereas para contrastar, despite con sustantivo, which o who entre comas y un participio como built.

origin.text: Datos: tu barrio es pequeño pero muy animado; la biblioteca, que está en la esquina, siempre está llena de niños; la señora Rojas, que lleva la biblioteca, conoce a todos los vecinos; hay tráfico, pero el parque, construido el año pasado, es tranquilo, mientras que el centro es ruidoso.

prompt.es: Escribe una frase con whereas para comparar dos lugares.

answer.text: My neighbourhood is quiet, whereas the centre is noisy.
accepted: My neighbourhood is quiet, whereas the centre is noisy.
My neighbourhood is peaceful, whereas the centre is very noisy.
The centre is noisy, whereas my neighbourhood is quiet.

feedback.es: Whereas compara dos cosas distintas: un barrio tranquilo frente a un centro ruidoso.

origin.text: Datos: mi barrio es tranquilo; el centro es ruidoso.

prompt.es: Elige la frase correcta para dar un dato extra sobre Ana, una vecina.

choices.text: Ana, which family runs the shop, is my friend.
Ana, whose family runs the shop, is my friend.
Ana, that family runs the shop, is my friend.

feedback.es: Whose indica posesión y se usa con personas: la familia de Ana. Which no sirve para personas y that no va entre comas.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué dice la hablante de su barrio.

choices.text: It is big and has nothing.
It is big and has many places.
It is small but has many places.

feedback.es: Despite being small expresa el contraste: el barrio es pequeño, pero tiene muchos lugares útiles.

origin.audio: Despite being small, our neighbourhood has everything: a library, a market and a playground.

es: Recibir a una visita: dar la bienvenida, presentar lugares con datos extra, contrastar dos opciones y responder dudas con oraciones complejas.

teaching.en: Welcome to our neighbourhood, which is small but very lively.
teaching.es: Bienvenido a nuestro barrio, que es pequeño pero muy animado.
teaching.explanationEs: Welcome to + lugar abre la visita. Which añade un dato extra del barrio.
teaching.audioText: Welcome to our neighbourhood, which is small but very lively.

teaching.en: I recommend the old market, which opens at seven.
teaching.es: Te recomiendo el mercado antiguo, que abre a las siete.
teaching.explanationEs: I recommend + lugar. El dato extra ayuda a decidir.
teaching.audioText: I recommend the old market, which opens at seven.

teaching.en: The tour, starting at the main square, takes one hour.
teaching.es: El recorrido, que empieza en la plaza principal, dura una hora.
teaching.explanationEs: Starting es un -ing entre comas: equivale a which starts.
teaching.audioText: The tour, starting at the main square, takes one hour.

teaching.en: Although the museum is expensive, the ticket is worth it.
teaching.es: Aunque el museo es caro, la entrada vale la pena.
teaching.explanationEs: Worth it = vale la pena. Although contrasta el precio con la recomendación.
teaching.audioText: Although the museum is expensive, the ticket is worth it.

teaching.en: The entrance, which is on the left, is free for every visitor.
teaching.es: La entrada, que está a la izquierda, es gratis para todos los visitantes.
teaching.explanationEs: Entrance es el lugar por donde se entra; ticket es el papel que pagas.
segments: The entrance, which is on the
left, is free for every visitor.
teaching.audioText: The entrance, which is on the left, is free for every visitor.

teaching.en: People who enjoy walking will love the route along the river.
teaching.es: A quienes disfrutan caminando les encantará la ruta junto al río.
teaching.explanationEs: Who sin comas: no son todas las personas, solo las que disfrutan caminando.
segments: People who enjoy walking will love
teaching.audioText: People who enjoy walking will love the route along the river.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué frase das la bienvenida a una visita?

choices.text: Welcome in our neighbourhood!
Welcome to our neighbourhood!
Welcome at our neighbourhood!

feedback.es: Welcome to + lugar es la fórmula habitual. Welcome in y welcome at son calcos que no se usan así.

hint.es: Después de welcome va la preposición de dirección.

prompt.es: Completa: «Recomiendo visitar el mercado antiguo.»

feedback.es: Recommend va seguido de -ing: I recommend visiting. No lleva to + verbo.

hint.es: Falta un -ing; no se usa to.

origin.text: I recommend ___ the old market.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Aunque la torre es cara, vale la pena.»

answer.text: Although the tower is expensive it is worth it

feedback.es: Although abre el contraste y it is worth it cierra la idea: la torre es cara, pero vale la pena.

hint.es: Empieza con el conector de contraste.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cuánto dura el recorrido.

choices.text: About 30 minutes.
About two hours.
About 60 minutes.

feedback.es: La ruta tarda one hour, es decir, unos 60 minutos. El dato extra entre comas dice cómo va la ruta.

origin.audio: Welcome! The tour starts at ten, and the route, which follows the river, takes one hour.

prompt.es: Completa: «La entrada, que cuesta cinco dólares, incluye la visita guiada.»

feedback.es: Which se refiere a una cosa, la entrada, y abre el dato extra entre comas.

origin.text: The ticket, ___ costs five dollars, includes the tour.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase compara dos lugares?

choices.text: The square is crowded, whereas the library is empty.
Although the square is crowded, whereas the library is empty.
The square is crowded despite the library is empty.

feedback.es: Whereas compara la plaza llena y la biblioteca vacía con sujeto + verbo. Although y whereas no se juntan, y despite no admite sujeto + verbo.

origin.text: The square is crowded. The library is empty.

prompt.es: Recibe a una visita: bienvenida, dos lugares con datos extra, contraste y recomendación.

answer.text: Welcome to our neighbourhood! The market, which opens at seven, is lively, whereas the library, which is on the corner, is peaceful. Although the market is crowded, it is worth visiting. I recommend visiting the market first. After that, the library is perfect for a quiet afternoon. Enjoy your visit!
accepted: Welcome to our neighbourhood! The market, which opens at seven, is lively, whereas the library, which is on the corner, is peaceful. Although the market is crowded, it is worth visiting. I recommend visiting the market first. After that, the library is perfect for a quiet afternoon. Enjoy your visit!

Welcome to our neighbourhood! Although the library, which is on the corner, is quiet, the market, which opens at seven, is more lively. I recommend the market. It is worth visiting, although it is crowded.

feedback.es: Un recorrido claro da la bienvenida, presenta los lugares con which, contrasta con whereas o although y termina recomendando.

origin.text: Datos: el mercado abre a las siete y es muy animado, aunque está lleno de gente; la biblioteca está en la esquina y es tranquila. Recomiendas visitar primero el mercado y luego la biblioteca.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué dice el guía sobre el museo.

choices.text: It is cheap, so it is a bad visit.
It is expensive, but a good visit.
It is closed for children.

feedback.es: Although marca el contraste: el museo es caro, pero vale la pena. No dice que sea malo.

origin.audio: Is the museum worth it? Although the ticket is expensive, it is worth it, because the entrance is free for children.

prompt.es: Completa: «Hicimos pintar la entrada antes de que llegaran los visitantes.»

feedback.es: Encargar un trabajo es had + objeto + participio: the entrance painted.

origin.text: We had the entrance ___ before the visitors arrived.

prompt.es: ¿Qué parte es un dato añadido?

choices.text: that crosses the river
is famous
overlooking the harbour

feedback.es: Overlooking the harbour va entre comas: es un dato extra. That crosses the river identifica el puente.

origin.text: The bridge that crosses the river is old. The tower, overlooking the harbour, is famous.

prompt.es: Elige la frase correcta para «A pesar de la lluvia, la visita fue genial».

choices.text: Despite the rain, the visit was great.
Despite it rained, the visit was great.
Although the rain, the visit was great.

feedback.es: Despite + sustantivo (the rain) es correcto. Despite it rained lleva sujeto + verbo y although the rain lleva solo un sustantivo.

prompt.es: Responde con although: el museo es caro, pero vale la pena.

answer.text: Although the museum is expensive, it is worth visiting.
accepted: Although the museum is expensive, it is worth visiting.
Although the museum is expensive, it is worth it.

feedback.es: Although contrasta el precio con la recomendación. Con worth, el verbo va en -ing: worth visiting.

origin.text: La visita pregunta si el museo vale la pena. Respondes: es caro, pero vale la pena visitarlo.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué le pasó a la visitante.

choices.text: She lost her way.
Someone took her phone.
She broke her phone.

feedback.es: Had her phone stolen cuenta algo malo que le ocurrió: alguien le robó el teléfono en la estación.

origin.audio: Our visitor, who arrived yesterday, had her phone stolen at the station.
